findings.title: Target served over plaintext HTTP
findings.reason: The target was served over plaintext HTTP (http://127.0.0.1:8080/weak); no transport encryption protects the response or its cookies.
findings.impact: All traffic — including cookies, tokens and form data — is transmitted in the clear and can be read or modified by anyone on the network path.
findings.recommendation: Terminate TLS for this host and permanently redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

findings.title: CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' scripts
findings.reason: script-src allows 'unsafe-inline', so inline scripts and event handlers execute.
findings.impact: 'unsafe-inline' in a script directive permits inline <script> blocks and event handlers, which is exactly the capability an XSS payload needs — the policy stops being a meaningful mitigation.
findings.recommendation: Move inline scripts to external files, or adopt a nonce/hash based strict CSP with 'strict-dynamic' for third-party loaders.

findings.title: CSP directive uses a wildcard source
findings.reason: default-src contains the wildcard source '*', allowing resources from any matching origin.
findings.impact: A wildcard source lets the page load that resource type from any origin, so an attacker-controlled host is an acceptable source as far as the browser is concerned.
findings.recommendation: Replace '*' with the explicit origins the application actually needs.

findings.title: CSP directive uses a wildcard source
findings.reason: script-src contains the wildcard source '*', allowing resources from any matching origin.
findings.impact: A wildcard source lets the page load that resource type from any origin, so an attacker-controlled host is an acceptable source as far as the browser is concerned.
findings.recommendation: Replace '*' with the explicit origins the application actually needs.

findings.title: CSP allows a dangerous scheme source
findings.reason: Dangerous scheme source(s) in an executable context: script-src: data:.
findings.impact: data:, blob: or filesystem: in a script/object directive lets an attacker encode a payload directly into a URI and execute it, bypassing origin restrictions.
findings.recommendation: Remove data:/blob: from script-src and object-src; keep them only for img-src or media where genuinely required.

findings.title: CSP frame-ancestors allows any origin
findings.reason: frame-ancestors * allows any site to frame this page.
findings.impact: frame-ancestors * lets any site frame the page, which enables clickjacking and UI redress attacks against authenticated users.
findings.recommendation: Set frame-ancestors 'none' or list the specific origins allowed to embed the page.

findings.title: CORS wildcard combined with credentials
findings.reason: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is '*' while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is true.
findings.impact: A wildcard origin together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true is rejected by browsers but signals a misconfigured CORS layer; if the wildcard is ever replaced by origin reflection, any site could read authenticated responses.
findings.recommendation: Never combine credentials with a wildcard. Echo one validated origin and keep the allow-list short.
findings.remediation:
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Vary: Origin

findings.title: Cookie without Secure attribute (PHPSESSID)
findings.reason: Cookie 'PHPSESSID' is missing the Secure attribute.
findings.impact: The cookie can be transmitted over plaintext HTTP, so an on-path attacker or a single mixed-content request can capture it.
findings.recommendation: Add the Secure attribute to every cookie and serve the site exclusively over HTTPS.
findings.remediation: Set-Cookie: session=...; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

findings.title: SameSite=None cookie without Secure (tracking)
findings.reason: Cookie 'tracking' uses SameSite=None without the Secure attribute; browsers reject it.
findings.impact: SameSite=None requires Secure. Browsers reject the cookie, and if it is accepted anywhere it is sent cross-site over plaintext connections.
findings.recommendation: Always pair SameSite=None with Secure, and question whether cross-site delivery is really needed.

findings.title: HSTS max-age is too short
findings.reason: max-age is 300 seconds (~0 days); at least 31536000 (1 year) is recommended.
findings.impact: A short max-age shrinks the window in which the browser enforces HTTPS. Once it expires the next navigation can be downgraded to HTTP again.
findings.recommendation: Use max-age=31536000 (one year). Ramp up gradually (300 → 86400 → 31536000) if the estate is still being migrated.

findings.title: CSP allows 'unsafe-eval'
findings.reason: script-src allows 'unsafe-eval'.
findings.impact: 'unsafe-eval' re-enables eval(), new Function() and string timers, giving injected content a direct route from data to executable code.
findings.recommendation: Remove 'unsafe-eval' and migrate templating/JSON parsing away from eval-based helpers (use JSON.parse and pre-compiled templates).

findings.title: CSP does not restrict object-src
findings.value: default-src * 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'; script-src * 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' data:; style-src * 'unsafe-inline'; img-src *; frame-ancestors *; report-uri /csp-report
findings.reason: object-src (via default-src) is * 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' instead of 'none'.
findings.impact: Plugin content (<object>, <embed>, <applet>) can execute scripts in the page's context and has historically been used to bypass CSP entirely.
findings.recommendation: Add object-src 'none' — virtually no modern application needs plugin content.

findings.title: CSP does not restrict base-uri
findings.value: default-src * 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'; script-src * 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' data:; style-src * 'unsafe-inline'; img-src *; frame-ancestors *; report-uri /csp-report
findings.reason: base-uri is not set (it does not fall back to default-src).
findings.impact: Without base-uri an injected <base> tag can re-point every relative URL on the page (scripts, forms, links) at an attacker-controlled host.
findings.recommendation: Add base-uri 'self' (or 'none' for pages with no relative-base requirements).

findings.title: X-Frame-Options uses obsolete ALLOW-FROM
findings.reason: ALLOW-FROM is not supported by modern browsers, so the page is effectively unprotected.
findings.impact: ALLOW-FROM was never implemented by Chrome/Safari and was removed from Firefox, so the directive provides no protection in current browsers.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with CSP frame-ancestors listing the permitted embedding origins.

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options
findings.reason: X-Content-Type-Options was not returned.
findings.impact: Without nosniff, browsers may MIME-sniff responses and execute a user-uploaded or text response as script or stylesheet.
findings.recommendation: Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every response and make sure Content-Type values are correct.

findings.title: Weak Referrer-Policy value
findings.reason: Effective policy 'unsafe-url': Sends the full URL (path and query) to every destination, including plaintext HTTP origins.
findings.impact: This policy sends full URLs (potentially including session identifiers, reset tokens or internal paths) to third parties, and some variants leak over plaintext downgrades.
findings.recommendation: Switch to strict-origin-when-cross-origin, same-origin or no-referrer.

findings.title: Cookie without Secure attribute (tracking)
findings.reason: Cookie 'tracking' is missing the Secure attribute.
findings.impact: The cookie can be transmitted over plaintext HTTP, so an on-path attacker or a single mixed-content request can capture it.
findings.recommendation: Add the Secure attribute to every cookie and serve the site exclusively over HTTPS.
findings.remediation: Set-Cookie: session=...; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

findings.title: Cookie without HttpOnly attribute (PHPSESSID)
findings.reason: Cookie 'PHPSESSID' is readable by JavaScript (no HttpOnly attribute). The name suggests it carries session state.
findings.impact: JavaScript can read this cookie, so a single XSS flaw turns into full session theft.
findings.recommendation: Add HttpOnly to all cookies that do not need to be read by client-side scripts.
findings.remediation: Set-Cookie: session=...; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

findings.title: HSTS does not cover subdomains
findings.reason: The policy does not include subdomains.
findings.impact: Without includeSubDomains an attacker can target a forgotten subdomain over HTTP and set or read domain-scoped cookies from there.
findings.recommendation: Add includeSubDomains after verifying that every subdomain (including internal ones) is reachable over HTTPS.

findings.title: CSP style-src allows 'unsafe-inline'
findings.reason: style-src allows 'unsafe-inline' for stylesheets.
findings.impact: Inline styles enable CSS-based data exfiltration and UI redressing tricks, though the impact is lower than for scripts.
findings.recommendation: Move inline styles into stylesheets or apply nonces/hashes to style blocks.

findings.title: CSP does not restrict form-action
findings.value: default-src * 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'; script-src * 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' data:; style-src * 'unsafe-inline'; img-src *; frame-ancestors *; report-uri /csp-report
findings.reason: form-action is not set, so form submissions are unrestricted.
findings.impact: Without form-action an injected or modified form can post user credentials to an attacker-controlled endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Add form-action 'self' (plus any legitimate payment/SSO endpoints).

findings.title: Missing Permissions-Policy
findings.reason: No Permissions-Policy header was returned.
findings.impact: Powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, payment) are left at their default availability for the page and for any embedded third-party frames.
findings.recommendation: Send a deny-by-default Permissions-Policy and only enable what the app needs.
findings.remediation: Permissions-Policy: accelerometer=(), camera=(), geolocation=(), gyroscope=(), magnetometer=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=()

findings.title: Missing Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy
findings.reason: No Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header was returned.
findings.impact: Without COOP, a window opened by (or opening) this page keeps a cross-origin reference to it, enabling XS-Leaks and tab-nabbing style attacks.
findings.recommendation: Send Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin (use same-origin-allow-popups when OAuth popups are required).

findings.title: Missing Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy
findings.reason: No Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy header was returned.
findings.impact: CORP tells the browser who may embed this resource. Without it, responses can be pulled into cross-origin documents and abused for side-channel (Spectre-class) leaks.
findings.recommendation: Send Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin for private resources, same-site for shared internal assets, cross-origin only for public CDN content.

findings.title: CORS allows unsafe methods broadly
findings.reason: Cross-origin callers may use DELETE, PUT, TRACE.
findings.impact: Allowing every method (including wildcards or state-changing verbs) from other origins widens the CSRF/abuse surface of the API.
findings.recommendation: List only the methods the endpoint actually implements.

findings.title: CORS allows arbitrary request headers
findings.reason: Access-Control-Allow-Headers is '*', allowing any custom request header cross-origin.
findings.impact: A wildcard header allow-list lets cross-origin callers send custom headers such as Authorization or X-Requested-With, which some backends treat as trusted.
findings.recommendation: Enumerate the accepted headers explicitly.

findings.title: Cookie without HttpOnly attribute (tracking)
findings.reason: Cookie 'tracking' is readable by JavaScript (no HttpOnly attribute).
findings.impact: JavaScript can read this cookie, so a single XSS flaw turns into full session theft.
findings.recommendation: Add HttpOnly to all cookies that do not need to be read by client-side scripts.
findings.remediation: Set-Cookie: session=...; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

findings.title: Cookie without SameSite attribute (PHPSESSID)
findings.reason: Cookie 'PHPSESSID' does not set SameSite explicitly.
findings.impact: Cross-site requests may carry this cookie depending on the browser's default, which keeps classic CSRF viable on older clients.
findings.recommendation: Set SameSite=Lax (or Strict for sensitive session cookies) explicitly.

findings.title: Cookie scoped to a broad parent domain (PHPSESSID)
findings.reason: Cookie 'PHPSESSID' is scoped to the parent domain 'localhost', so every subdomain receives it.
findings.impact: A cookie scoped to the registrable domain is sent to every subdomain, so a compromised or attacker-controlled subdomain can read or overwrite it.
findings.recommendation: Drop the Domain attribute to make the cookie host-only, or use the __Host- prefix.

findings.title: Server software version disclosed
findings.reason: The Server header exposes a specific version: HeaderSpecterDemo/1.0, nginx/1.18.0 (Ubuntu).
findings.impact: Exact software versions let an attacker map the target to known CVEs without touching the application, speeding up reconnaissance.
findings.recommendation: Suppress or genericise the Server banner (nginx: server_tokens off; Apache: ServerTokens Prod).

findings.title: Technology disclosed via X-Powered-By
findings.reason: X-Powered-By discloses: PHP/7.4.3.
findings.impact: The header advertises the application stack and often its exact version, which is pure reconnaissance value for an attacker.
findings.recommendation: Remove the header (PHP: expose_php=Off; Express: app.disable('x-powered-by')).

findings.title: Framework version headers exposed
findings.reason: X-AspNet-Version discloses the framework version: 4.0.30319.
findings.impact: ASP.NET/MVC version headers identify the exact framework build in use.
findings.recommendation: Remove them via <httpRuntime enableVersionHeader="false" /> and MvcHandler.DisableMvcResponseHeader = true.

findings.title: X-XSS-Protection filtering enabled
findings.reason: X-XSS-Protection is set to '1; mode=block'; the legacy auditor is removed from modern browsers and was itself a source of vulnerabilities.
findings.impact: Value '1' without mode=block enables legacy filtering that was itself exploitable for XS-leaks and content injection in older browsers.
findings.recommendation: Set X-XSS-Protection: 0 and deploy a CSP instead.

findings.title: Potentially sensitive response is cacheable
findings.reason: The response sets cookies but does not use Cache-Control: no-store, so a shared cache may store user-specific content.
findings.impact: The response sets cookies or looks user-specific, yet allows shared/public caching, which can leak one user's content to another via a proxy or CDN.
findings.recommendation: Send Cache-Control: no-store (plus private where appropriate) for user-specific responses.

findings.title: HSTS preload not requested
findings.reason: The policy does not request HSTS preloading.
findings.impact: Without preloading, the very first visit from a fresh browser profile can still be made over HTTP (trust-on-first-use gap).
findings.recommendation: Once max-age >= 31536000 and includeSubDomains is set, add the preload token and submit the domain at hstspreload.org. Preloading is hard to undo — plan first.

findings.title: HSTS sent over plaintext HTTP
findings.reason: The HSTS header was returned over HTTP, where browsers ignore it.
findings.impact: HSTS headers received over HTTP are ignored by browsers, so the policy is not actually applied.
findings.recommendation: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS first and send the HSTS header on the HTTPS response.

findings.title: CSP uses deprecated report-uri only
findings.reason: Only the deprecated report-uri directive is configured.
findings.impact: report-uri is deprecated in favour of the Reporting API; newer browsers prefer report-to and may drop report-uri support.
findings.recommendation: Keep report-uri for legacy clients but add report-to with a Reporting-Endpoints header.

findings.title: Missing Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy
findings.reason: No Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy header was returned.
findings.impact: Without COEP the document cannot become cross-origin isolated, so powerful APIs (SharedArrayBuffer, high-resolution timers) stay disabled and Spectre-class mitigations are weaker.
findings.recommendation: Send Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp (or credentialless) together with COOP: same-origin when you need cross-origin isolation.

findings.title: Long-lived persistent cookie (tracking)
findings.reason: Cookie 'tracking' persists for roughly 730 days.
findings.impact: Very long lifetimes extend the window in which a stolen cookie remains valid.
findings.recommendation: Prefer short-lived session cookies with server-side revocation for authentication state.

findings.title: Missing X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies
findings.reason: X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies was not returned.
findings.impact: Legacy Adobe clients fall back to looking for a /crossdomain.xml policy file.
findings.recommendation: Send X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies: none (defence in depth, zero cost).

findings.title: X-XSS-Protection filtering enabled
findings.reason: X-XSS-Protection is set to '1'; the legacy auditor is removed from modern browsers and was itself a source of vulnerabilities.
findings.impact: Value '1' without mode=block enables legacy filtering that was itself exploitable for XS-leaks and content injection in older browsers.
findings.recommendation: Set X-XSS-Protection: 0 and deploy a CSP instead.

findings.title: Permissive X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies
findings.reason: X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies is 'all' instead of 'none'.
findings.impact: Allowing cross-domain policy files lets legacy Adobe clients (Flash/Acrobat) read data from this origin.
findings.recommendation: Set X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies: none unless a legacy client requires otherwise.

findings.title: Deprecated Feature-Policy header in use
findings.reason: The deprecated Feature-Policy header is still being sent.
findings.impact: Feature-Policy has been renamed to Permissions-Policy; modern browsers ignore the old header and its syntax differs.
findings.recommendation: Emit Permissions-Policy (structured syntax). Keep Feature-Policy only if you must support very old browsers.

findings.title: Missing Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy
findings.reason: No Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy header was returned.
findings.impact: Without COEP the document cannot become cross-origin isolated, so powerful APIs (SharedArrayBuffer, high-resolution timers) stay disabled and Spectre-class mitigations are weaker.
findings.recommendation: Send Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp (or credentialless) together with COOP: same-origin when you need cross-origin isolation.

findings.title: Infrastructure detail disclosed via Via
findings.reason: Via exposes infrastructure detail: 1.1 internal-cache-03.dc1.local.
findings.impact: Headers such as Via, X-Backend-Server or X-Served-By reveal internal hostnames and proxy topology that help an attacker map the environment.
findings.recommendation: Strip internal routing headers at the edge before responses leave the perimeter.

findings.title: Generator / CMS disclosed
findings.reason: X-Generator discloses: Drupal 7 (https://www.drupal.org).
findings.impact: Identifying the CMS and version narrows down which plugin vulnerabilities to try.
findings.recommendation: Disable generator headers/meta tags in the CMS configuration.

findings.title: Deprecated Expect-CT header present
findings.reason: The obsolete Expect-CT header is still sent.
findings.impact: Certificate Transparency is now enforced by browsers automatically; Expect-CT is obsolete and ignored.
findings.recommendation: Remove the header.

findings.title: Legacy Pragma header present
findings.reason: The HTTP/1.0 Pragma header is still present.
findings.impact: Pragma: no-cache is an HTTP/1.0 relic. It is harmless but indicates cache policy may not have been reviewed for modern clients.
findings.recommendation: Rely on Cache-Control; keep Pragma only if HTTP/1.0 intermediaries still matter.

findings.title: No Cache-Control header
findings.reason: No Cache-Control header was returned.
findings.impact: Without an explicit policy, heuristic caching by browsers and shared proxies decides how long the response is stored.
findings.recommendation: Set an explicit policy: no-store for authenticated pages, immutable long max-age for fingerprinted static assets.

checks.detail: none returned — resource is same-origin only

tls_checks.detail: not in use — traffic is sent in clear text

recommendations: Terminate TLS for this host and permanently redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
Deploy a restrictive CSP tailored to the application's real resource needs.
Send CSP frame-ancestors 'none' (modern) and X-Frame-Options: DENY (legacy clients) for pages that must never be framed.
Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every response and make sure Content-Type values are correct.
Remove Public-Key-Pins entirely; use Certificate Transparency monitoring and CAA records instead.
Send Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or no-referrer for the most privacy-sensitive applications).

Send Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin (use same-origin-allow-popups when OAuth popups are required).

findings.title: Target served over plaintext HTTP
findings.reason: The target was served over plaintext HTTP (http://127.0.0.1:8080/api); no transport encryption protects the response or its cookies.
findings.impact: All traffic — including cookies, tokens and form data — is transmitted in the clear and can be read or modified by anyone on the network path.
findings.recommendation: Terminate TLS for this host and permanently redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy
findings.reason: No Content-Security-Policy header was returned.
findings.impact: No CSP was detected, so the browser has no policy-level defence against injected scripts, unexpected resource loads or data exfiltration to attacker domains.
findings.recommendation: Deploy a restrictive CSP tailored to the application's real resource needs. Start in Report-Only mode, collect violations, then enforce.
findings.remediation: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'

findings.title: CORS reflects an arbitrary origin with credentials
findings.reason: The server reflected the probe origin https://headerspecter.invalid and allows credentials, so any site could read authenticated responses.
findings.impact: The server echoed the probe origin back and allows credentials, so any attacker site can make authenticated cross-origin requests and read the responses — a direct account-data disclosure path.
findings.recommendation: Validate Origin against a strict allow-list before echoing it, and only enable credentials for origins you control.
findings.remediation:
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Vary: Origin

findings.title: No clickjacking protection
findings.reason: Neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors was returned.
findings.impact: Neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors was returned, so the page can be embedded in a hidden iframe and used for clickjacking against logged-in users.
findings.recommendation: Send CSP frame-ancestors 'none' (modern) and X-Frame-Options: DENY (legacy clients) for pages that must never be framed.

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options
findings.reason: X-Content-Type-Options was not returned.
findings.impact: Without nosniff, browsers may MIME-sniff responses and execute a user-uploaded or text response as script or stylesheet.
findings.recommendation: Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every response and make sure Content-Type values are correct.

findings.title: Missing Referrer-Policy
findings.reason: No Referrer-Policy header was returned.
findings.impact: Browser defaults vary. Full URLs — including path, query string, tokens and internal identifiers — can leak to third-party sites through the Referer header.
findings.recommendation: Send Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or no-referrer for the most privacy-sensitive applications).

findings.title: Missing Permissions-Policy
findings.reason: No Permissions-Policy header was returned.
findings.impact: Powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, payment) are left at their default availability for the page and for any embedded third-party frames.
findings.recommendation: Send a deny-by-default Permissions-Policy and only enable what the app needs.
findings.remediation: Permissions-Policy: accelerometer=(), camera=(), geolocation=(), gyroscope=(), magnetometer=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=()

findings.title: Missing Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy
findings.reason: No Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header was returned.
findings.impact: Without COOP, a window opened by (or opening) this page keeps a cross-origin reference to it, enabling XS-Leaks and tab-nabbing style attacks.
findings.recommendation: Send Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin (use same-origin-allow-popups when OAuth popups are required).

findings.title: Missing Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy
findings.reason: No Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy header was returned.
findings.impact: CORP tells the browser who may embed this resource. Without it, responses can be pulled into cross-origin documents and abused for side-channel (Spectre-class) leaks.
findings.recommendation: Send Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin for private resources, same-site for shared internal assets, cross-origin only for public CDN content.

findings.title: Dynamic CORS response is missing Vary: Origin
findings.reason: The allowed origin depends on the request but the response does not include Vary: Origin, so caches may reuse it for other origins.
findings.impact: When the allowed origin depends on the request but Vary: Origin is absent, shared caches and CDNs can serve one origin's CORS headers to another origin.
findings.recommendation: Add Vary: Origin to every response whose CORS headers depend on the request origin.

findings.title: Server software version disclosed
findings.reason: The Server header exposes a specific version: HeaderSpecterDemo/1.0.
findings.impact: Exact software versions let an attacker map the target to known CVEs without touching the application, speeding up reconnaissance.
findings.recommendation: Suppress or genericise the Server banner (nginx: server_tokens off; Apache: ServerTokens Prod).

findings.title: Missing Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy
findings.reason: No Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy header was returned.
findings.impact: Without COEP the document cannot become cross-origin isolated, so powerful APIs (SharedArrayBuffer, high-resolution timers) stay disabled and Spectre-class mitigations are weaker.
findings.recommendation: Send Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp (or credentialless) together with COOP: same-origin when you need cross-origin isolation.

findings.title: CORS exposes additional response headers
findings.reason: Response headers exposed to cross-origin scripts: X-Internal-Request-Id, X-Debug-Token.
findings.impact: Exposed headers become readable by cross-origin scripts; wildcards may reveal internal or sensitive metadata.
findings.recommendation: Expose only the headers clients genuinely need.

findings.title: Infrastructure detail disclosed via X-Backend-Server
findings.reason: X-Backend-Server exposes infrastructure detail: api-node-7.internal.lab.
findings.impact: Headers such as Via, X-Backend-Server or X-Served-By reveal internal hostnames and proxy topology that help an attacker map the environment.
findings.recommendation: Strip internal routing headers at the edge before responses leave the perimeter.

findings.title: Missing X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies
findings.reason: X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies was not returned.
findings.impact: Legacy Adobe clients fall back to looking for a /crossdomain.xml policy file.
findings.recommendation: Send X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies: none (defence in depth, zero cost).
